rationale:
runtimes/csharp/Telemetry.cs: The proto field speed_mps changed from float to double, so the generated C# property SpeedMps is now double. The explicit cast (float)request.Speed narrowed the input precision; removing the cast preserves the full binary64 precision through serialization. The dictionary assignment (line 13) and comparison (line 14) already work with double and remain unchanged. The request.Speed is already double (line 19).
runtimes/python/telemetry_runtime.py: The schema change widens the wire representation of speed_mps from float32 to float64 (proto3 float -> double). In Python, both protobuf float and double fields map to the built-in float type (IEEE 754 binary64). The generated bindings automatically handle the widened wire format; no source changes are required. The threshold 30.0 and observation key 'speed_mps' remain unchanged. Since the runtime already uses Python float for the field, the precision improvement is transparent and no explicit narrowing or conversion code exists to remove.
runtimes/typescript/telemetry.ts: The TypeScript runtime file uses the generated protobuf bindings (ts-proto) which handle the wire encoding/decoding. The schema change from float to double in the .proto file will cause the generated TypeScript bindings to use `number` for both (since TypeScript only has `number` for binary64). The source code uses `entity.speedMps` and `speedMps` property names which are determined by the generated bindings, not the wire type. No changes to this hand-written runtime file are needed; regeneration of the generated bindings from the updated .proto will handle the wire format change automatically. The strict >30 threshold and observation key `speed_mps` are preserved as-is.
assumptions: runtimes/csharp/Telemetry.cs: The protobuf code generator produces SpeedMps as double when the schema uses double.
runtimes/csharp/Telemetry.cs: The Threshold comparison > 30.0 uses double literal and is correct for meters per second.
runtimes/csharp/Telemetry.cs: TelemetryRequest.Speed is double as shown on line 19.
runtimes/csharp/Telemetry.cs: No other producer/consumer narrowing is required.
runtimes/python/telemetry_runtime.py: The regenerated protobuf bindings (vehicle_pb2) will expose speed_mps as a float property, matching the new double wire type.
runtimes/python/telemetry_runtime.py: No external consumers depend on the previous float32 wire encoding; coordinated rollout is handled separately.
runtimes/typescript/telemetry.ts: The generated TypeScript bindings (ts-proto) will be regenerated from the updated .proto file
runtimes/typescript/telemetry.ts: ts-proto maps both float and double to TypeScript `number` (binary64)
runtimes/typescript/telemetry.ts: The property names `vehicleId` and `speedMps` in the generated bindings remain unchanged
